blueprint_phase_a_v4.evidence: 441 released OSCAR generated-left-view episodes from 63 sessions and 7 policies
blueprint_phase_a_v4.protocol: 32 generated-only frames scored independently per episode with task-progress, artifact, uncertainty, and abstention fields
blueprint_phase_a_v4.aggregation: mean safety-adjusted progress followed by policy ordering
blueprint_phase_a_v4.result: Spearman 0.357, Kendall tau-b 0.238, pairwise 0.619; all rank and selective-usefulness gates failed

oscar_paper.evidence: 65 manually retained sessions by 7 policies with acceptable estimated camera calibration
oscar_paper.protocol: 32 native-resolution frames for episode success plus direct two-video within-session pairwise judgments
oscar_paper.aggregation: 1365 pairwise preferences aggregated with Bradley-Terry scores
oscar_paper.key_non_equivalence: Blueprint used GPT-5 mini, 63 sessions, single-video independent scoring, and no direct pairwise judge. The released public halves are 640x480 left-view videos, whereas OSCAR reports private evaluator frames at native 512x288, so the new diagnostic shares the published view and sampling concept but is not byte-identical.

roboworld_paper.evidence: 4186 closed-loop rollouts, 8 policies, two fixed views plus wrist view
roboworld_paper.protocol: six-level progress/world-model-error rubric; one frame per second; two 15-frame segments; maximum segment score
roboworld_paper.reported_result: Spearman 0.970; Pearson 0.989 with GPT-4o and 0.944 with Gemini-2.5-Flash
roboworld_paper.key_non_equivalence: purpose-trained closed-loop multi-view WAM and far larger rollout matrix; paper reports occasional VLM hallucinated success on static scenes

sc3_eval_paper.evidence: seven pi0.5 checkpoints, 36-37 trajectories each, three separately scored criteria, three views
sc3_eval_paper.judge: blinded human annotators for main results; Gemini-3.1-Pro only an appendix substitution diagnostic
sc3_eval_paper.protocol: Cosmos3-Nano initialized model trained on 381 task-specific hours with forward-inverse and cross-view consistency plus action-recovery early termination
sc3_eval_paper.reported_result: closed-loop Pearson 0.929 and MMRV 0.119 over 21 checkpoint-criterion points
sc3_eval_paper.key_non_equivalence: task-specific training on 32 GB200 GPUs and human main scoring; not base Cosmos3 acting as a VLM judge

ctrl_world_paper.evidence: three policies on a separately constructed DROID setup
ctrl_world_paper.protocol: closed-loop multi-view WAM trained on 95k DROID trajectories with pose memory, frame-level action conditioning, and learned joint-velocity adapter
ctrl_world_paper.reported_result: instruction-following rankings aligned with real rollouts; low-level success was underestimated
ctrl_world_paper.key_non_equivalence: three-policy task-specific human-scored result, not an off-the-shelf automated VLM benchmark

worldeval_paper.evidence: four policies across task-specific real and generated evaluation on an ALOHA-style bimanual platform
worldeval_paper.protocol: 14B video model lightly fine-tuned on 1400 task-platform trajectories using policy latent actions
worldeval_paper.reported_result: average Pearson 0.942 and MMRV 0.044 on three RoboTwin-derived tasks
worldeval_paper.key_non_equivalence: small policy count and task/platform-specific fine-tuning; metrics are not directly comparable to Blueprint's seven-policy DROID rank vector

answer_to_better_vlm_question: A stronger judge may improve Blueprint. The frozen diagnostic therefore compares full GPT-5 with OSCAR-inspired direct pairwise judgments, the newer lower-cost GPT-5.4 mini snapshot on the same 32-frame inputs, native-video Gemini 3.6 Flash, and the open Cosmos3-Nano Reasoner. Cosmos Reasoner may diagnose the released OSCAR videos, but it cannot be the sole evaluator of native Cosmos-generated rollouts because that would violate the independent-evaluator boundary. None can receive confirmatory credit on the now-exposed snapshot.
claim_boundary: Primary-paper methodology comparison. Headline numbers are not treated as interchangeable because policies, tasks, views, world models, scoring units, and aggregation differ.
